description.value: Faithful design-doc projection of the 2026-02-18 architecture review. Operating principles: (1) every element corresponds to something the conversation actually decided — architectural-review remarks that merely cite an existing domain rule as context are not extracted as new rules; (2) Building Blocks existing in code but invisible to the domain scan are not modelled — decisions about them attach to the nearest scan-visible carrier (an existing aggregate / factory / repository / module); (3) read-side query repositories already exist (Sales.OnlineOrdering.OrderDetailsFinder, Sales.WholesaleOrdering.OrderDetailsFinder) and are reused as the consumers of the new OrderReadModel projection. The two decisions captured: (a) Order persistence — Marten Document Store on the write side and EF Core read side via Marten inline projections; (b) Sales→RiskManagement integration stays synchronous and in-process under an explicit co-deployment assumption with revisit triggers.

Flat denormalised relational projection of Order for query workloads — header columns, denormalised line summaries, pricing totals — populated by Marten inline projections atomically with the document save by Sales.Orders.Repository. Indexed for filtering, sorting and pagination by EF Core. Owned by Sales.Orders; not a separate aggregate; it has no behaviour of its own. Consumed by the existing read-side repositories Sales.OnlineOrdering.OrderDetailsFinder and Sales.WholesaleOrdering.OrderDetailsFinder — this design doc does not introduce a new query Building Block, only the projection they read from.

name.value: Read model stays in sync within the same transaction

description.value: Verifies the inline-projection guarantee on the read side — a follow-up query observes the new row immediately.

when.value: Sales.Orders.Repository saves the Order document via Marten

then.value:
the Marten inline projection updates the OrderReadModel row in the same database transaction
And a follow-up read for the new Order via the existing OrderDetailsFinder returns the projected data immediately, without observable lag

description.value: Trigger: any persistence operation on Order via Sales.Orders.Repository. Pre: a coherent aggregate state exists in memory. Algorithm: load and save the entire JSONB document atomically; mutate only via aggregate methods, never through external table updates. Post: aggregate state on disk matches the in-memory state at commit. Edge cases: read-model projections must be written in the same transaction (inline) so reads and writes never observe a torn state; partial reads or partial writes of the aggregate are not allowed.

name.value: Order load and save is whole-aggregate

description.value: Verifies the Consistency rule that the Order aggregate is treated as a single load/save unit on the document store.

given.value: an existing Order with three line items has been persisted

when.value: an aggregate command updates one line item

then.value:
the entire Order aggregate is reloaded from its JSONB document
And after the update, the entire aggregate is written back as a single document in one transaction
And no external write touches Order tables outside the aggregate boundary
